extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (students, researchers, and developers working in computational algebra/cryptography)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation (Appendix D) listing SINGULAR library procedures (crypto.lib, hyperel.lib, teachstd.lib, weierstr.lib, rootsmr.lib) with their usage, return values, notes, and examples for computational-algebra tasks and teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: calculate_ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: calculate_ordering(num1, primitive, mod1). Return x so that primitive^x == num1 mod mod1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: mod1=33, primitive=14, num1=5 → calculate_ordering(...) → 3. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: is_primitive_root
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: is_primitive_root(primitive, mod1). Return 1 if primitive is a primitive root modulo mod1, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: is_primitive_root(3,7) → 1; is_primitive_root(2,7) → 0. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: find_first_primitive_root
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: find_first_primitive_root(mod1). Return the first primitive root modulo mod1, 0 if no root can be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: find_first_primitive_root(7) → 3; find_first_primitive_root(557) → 2. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: binary_add
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: binary_add(binary_list). Return binary encoded list increased by 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: binary_list = 1,0,1,1,1 → binary_add(...) → 1,1,0,0,0. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: inverse_modulus
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: inverse_modulus(num, mod1). Return inverse element of num modulo mod1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: inverse_modulus(5,13) → 8. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: is_prime
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: is_prime(n). Return 1 if n is prime, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: is_prime(10) → 0; is_prime(7) → 1. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: find_index
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: find_index(a, e). Return the list index of element e in list a. Returns 0 if e is not in a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: list a = 1,5,20,6,37; find_index(a,20) → 3; find_index(a,100) → 0. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: subset_sum01
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: subset_sum01(knapsack, solution). Returns binary list of positions of elements included in subset sum or 0 if no solution exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns first solution using smallest binary encoding; will not return multiple solutions. Examples: knapsack = [1,4,7,32]; subset_sum01(...,11) → 0,1,1,0 etc. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: subset_sum02
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: subset_sum02(knapsack, sol). Return binary list of positions of elements included in the subset sum or 0 if no solution exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example outcomes shown for knapsack [1,4,7,32] similar to subset_sum01. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: unbounded_knapsack
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: unbounded_knapsack(knapsack, profit, capacity). Return list of maximum profit for each capacity iteration (list[i] is max profit for capacity i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: knapsack=[5,2], profit=[10,3], capacity=5 → returned list shows profits up to capacity 6 in example. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: multidimensional_knapsack
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: multidimensional_knapsack(m, capacities, profits). Return binary list of positions of elements included in the optimal selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example uses a matrix m, capacities c, profits p and returns a binary selection list. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: naccache_stern_generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: naccache_stern_generation(key, primenum). Return a hard knapsack list (or 0 if generation fails).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: naccache_stern_generation(5,293) returns a list such as [85,164,117,44]. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: naccache_stern_encryption
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: naccache_stern_encryption(knapsack, message, primenum). Return an encrypted message as integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: example values for primenum and hardknapsack are obtained from generation example. Example returns 9945. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: naccache_stern_decryption
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: naccache_stern_decryption(knapsack, key, primenum, message). Return decrypted binary list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: input from prior generation/encryption returns binary message list. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: m_merkle_hellman_transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: m_merkle_hellman_transformation(knapsack, primitive, mod1). Return list containing a hard knapsack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example transforms a superincreasing knapsack into a hard knapsack with given primitive and modulus. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: m_merkle_hellman_encryption
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: m_merkle_hellman_encryption(knapsack, message). Return an encrypted message as integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works like merkle_hellman_encryption and is provided for consistency across crypto systems. Example returns 140. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: m_merkle_hellman_decryption
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: m_merkle_hellman_decryption(knapsack, primitive, mod1, message). Return decrypted binary list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates decryption using primitive and modulus from transformation example. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: merkle_hellman_encryption
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: merkle_hellman_encryption(knapsack, message). Return encrypted integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: hardknapsack [3,9,15,13], message [0,1,0,1] → 22. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: merkle_hellman_decryption
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: merkle_hellman_decryption(knapsack, key, mod1, message). Return decrypted binary list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: decrypt 22 with key=3, mod1=23 returns binary list [0,1,0,1]. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: super_increasing_knapsack
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: super_increasing_knapsack(ksize). Return a super-increasing knapsack list of given size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example for ksize 10 shows descending powers like 256,512,128,...,1. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: h_increasing_knapsack
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: h_increasing_knapsack(ksize, h). Return h-increasing knapsack list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: h_increasing_knapsack(10,5) returns sequence with h-increase pattern; shown values include 1,2,4,8,16,32,... and larger entries. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: injective_knapsack
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: injective_knapsack(ksize, kmaxelement). Return list of injective knapsacks with maximal element kmaxelement and size ksize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: injective_knapsack(3,9) returns many candidate knapsacks formatted in example output. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: calculate_max_sum
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: calculate_max_sum(a). Return sum of all elements in a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: list a = 1,5,3,2,12 → calculate_max_sum(a) → 23. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: set_is_injective
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: set_is_injective(a). Return 1 if a is injective, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: inj = 1,5,7,41 → returns 1; non_inj = 1,2,3,4 returns 0. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: is_h_injective
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: is_h_injective(a, h). Return 1 if a is h-injective, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: list h_inj = 1,2,4,10,17; is_h_injective(h_inj,3) → 1 because 1+2+4+10=17; is_h_injective(h_inj,4) → 0. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: is_fix_injective
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: is_fix_injective(a). Return 1 if a is fix-injective, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: fix_inj = 1,2,4,10,17 → returns 1 (17=10+2+4+1 with different numbers of addends); not_fix_inj = 1,2,3,4 → returns 0. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: three_elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: three_elements(out, iterations). Return: injective knapsack created with the three elements method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows applying three_elements to a super_increasing list and testing injectivity with set_is_injective. (From crypto.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: ishyper
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ishyper(h,f); h,f = poly. Return 1 if y^2 + h(x) y = f(x) is hyperelliptic, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests hyperellipticity over the basering and shows error messages. Example: ring R=7,x,dp; h=x; f=x^5+...; ishyper(h,f) → 1. (From hyperel.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: isoncurve
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isoncurve(P,h,f); h,f = poly; P = list. Return 1 if P is on the hyperelliptic curve y^2 + h(x) y = f(x), 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: P=2,3 with same h,f above returns 1. (From hyperel.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: chinrestp
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: chinrestp(b, moduli); b, moduli = list of polynomials. Return polynomial x such that x = b[i] mod moduli[i].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chinese remainder theorem for polynomials. Example returns combined polynomial for provided residues and moduli. (From hyperel.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: norm
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: norm(a,b,h,f). Return the norm of a(x)-b(x)y in IF[C].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: norm is a polynomial in one variable; curve C: y^2+h(x)y=f(x) defined over basering. Example returns polynomial -x^7+... (From hyperel.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: multi
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: multi(a,b,c,d,h,f). Return list L with L[1]-L[2]y = (a(x)-b(x)y)*(c(x)-d(x)y) in IF[C].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows multiplication result components for polynomials on hyperelliptic curve. (From hyperel.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: divisor
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: divisor(a,b,h,f); optional divisor(a,b,h,f,s) with s=0,1. Return list P representing divisor of (a(x)-b(x)y), optionally returning parameter s indicating irreducible polynomials occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If s != 0 returns parameter about irreducible polynomials; otherwise warnings displayed. Curve defined over basering. Example shows divisor output format. (From hyperel.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: gcddivisor
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: gcddivisor(p,q). Return list P representing gcd of two divisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates gcd of two divisors provided in rational representation. (From hyperel.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: semidiv
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: semidiv(D,h,f). Return list P. Important: Divisor D has to be semireduced. Computes divisor representation of D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computes *(P[size(P)][1],P[size(P)][2]) - (*)infty = div(D[1],D[2]). Example shows input D and returned P. (From hyperel.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: cantoradd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: cantoradd(D,Q,h,f). Return list P. Cantor's algorithm for composition: D and Q must be semireduced; computes semireduced divisor for sum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computes div(P[1],P[2]) = div(D[1],D[2]) + div(Q[1],Q[2]). Divisors defined over basering. Example returns components of resulting divisor. (From hyperel.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: cantorred
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: cantorred(D,h,f). Return list N. Cantor's algorithm - reduction: D must be semireduced; computes reduced divisor div(N[1],N[2])=div(D[1],D[2]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisors defined over basering. Example shows reduction result. (From hyperel.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: double
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: double(D,h,f). Return list Q = 2*D. Divisor D must be semireduced. Special case of Cantor's algorithm computing 2*div(D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computes reduced divisor for doubling. Example shows input reduced divisor and output. (From hyperel.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: cantormult
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: cantormult(m, D, h, f). Return res = m*D. Important: D must be semireduced; uses repeated doublings for faster computation. m is integer (bounded); for m<0 inverse is returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: cantormult(34, D, h, f) returns reduced divisor for 34*D. (From hyperel.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: ecart
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ecart(f); f poly or vector. Return the ecart e of f (type int).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows different rings and outputs: ecart((y+z+x+xyz)**2) returns 4 in ls ordering and 0 in dp. (From teachstd.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: tail
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tail(f); f poly or vector. Return f - lead(f), the tail of f (type poly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: tail((y+z+x+xyz)**2) returns different tails depending on monomial ordering. (From teachstd.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: sameComponent
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sameComponent(f,g); f,g poly or vector. Return 1 if f and g are of same type poly or vectors whose leading monomials involve the same module component, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate returns for various inputs comparing leading monomials/components. (From teachstd.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: leadmonomial
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: leadmonomial(f); f poly or vector. Return the leading monomial of f (type poly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: if f is vector and leadmonom(f)=m*gen(i) then leadmonomial = m. Example outputs leading monomial. (From teachstd.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: monomialLcm
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: monomialLcm(m,n); m,n of type poly or vector. Return least common multiple of leading monomials of m and n, type poly; returns 0 if different module components for vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition given by exponent-wise max; examples demonstrate outputs and zero cases. (From teachstd.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: spoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: spoly(f,g[,s]); f,g poly or vector, s int. Return the s-polynomial of f and g (poly or vector). If s!=0 returns symmetric s-polynomial (without division).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show different orderings and symmetric vs usual s-polys and vector cases. (From teachstd.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: minEcart
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: minEcart(T,h); T ideal or module, h poly or vector. Returns element g from T such that leadmonom(g) divides leadmonom(h) and ecart(g) is minimal with this property; returns 0 if T=0 or h=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show usage for ideal and module inputs returning appropriate minimal-ecart elements. (From teachstd.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: NFMora
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: NFMora(f,G[,s]); f poly or vector, G ideal or module, s int. Return the Mora normal form of f w.r.t. G (same type as f). If s!=0 symmetric s-polynomial is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows behaviour with printlevel settings and examples in different rings/orderings returning normal forms or 0. (From teachstd.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: prodcrit
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: prodcrit(f,g[,o]); f,g poly or vector, optional int o. Return 1 if product criterion applies in same module component, 2 if leads involve different components, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If product criterion applies we can delete (f,g) from pairset. Returns 0 if o positive integer given or can set default arg attribute. Examples given. (From teachstd.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: chaincrit
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: chaincrit(f,g,h); f,g,h poly or module. Return 1 if chain criterion applies, 0 else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If chain criterion applies to f,g,h we can delete (g,h) from pairset. Examples illustrate both polynomial and vector/module cases. (From teachstd.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: pairset
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: pairset(G); G ideal or module. Return a list L where L[1] is the pairset of G as list (not containing pairs for which product or chain criterion applies) and L[2] is intvec v counting how many product/chain criterion occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show returned pairset list and counts in both ideal and module contexts. (From teachstd.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: updatePairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: updatePairs(P,S,h); P list of pairs, S ideal or module, h poly or vector. Return list Q where Q[1] is P enlarged by pairs (f,h) for f in S that don't satisfy product/chain criterion, and Q[2] is intvec with counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate how updating pairset with new element h modifies pair list and counts. (From teachstd.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: standard(i[,s]); i = ideal or module, s int. Return a standard basis of i using generalized Mora’s algorithm (Buchberger’s algorithm for global orderings). If s!=0 symmetric s-polynomial (without division) is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows printlevel behaviour and examples returning standard bases for ideals and modules; multiple examples for different coefficient rings/orderings. (From teachstd.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: localstd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: localstd(id); id = ideal. Return a standard basis for a local degree ordering using Lazard’s method by homogenizing w.r.t. new variable local@t, computing SB w.r.t. dp(1),dp, then substituting local@t = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: useful to avoid cancellation of units and to enable option(contentSB) for local orderings. Long example shows many returned basis elements. (From teachstd.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: weierstrDiv
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: weierstrDiv(g,f,d); g,f = poly, d = integer. Assume f is T-general of finite order b; perform Weierstrass division of g by f up to order d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list l of two polynomials and an integer such that g = l[1]*f + l[2] with deg_T(l[2]) < b up to total degree d; l[3] is number of iterations used; if f not T-general returns (0,g). Works for any monomial ordering. Example included. (From weierstr.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: weierstrPrep
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: weierstrPrep(f,d); f = poly, d = integer. Assume f is T-general; perform Weierstrass preparation of f up to order d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list l where l[1] is a unit, l[2] is a Weierstrass polynomial (T^b + lower terms) up to total degree d, l[3] is iteration count; if f not T-general returns (0,0). Works for any monomial ordering. Example given. (From weierstr.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: lastvarGeneral
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: lastvarGeneral(f,d); f = poly. Return g obtained from f by a generic change of variables so that g is general of finite order b w.r.t. last ring variable T (i.e., g(0,...,0,T) = c*T^b + ... with c != 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works for any monomial ordering. Example demonstrates output. (From weierstr.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: generalOrder
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: generalOrder(f); f = poly. Return integer b if f is general of order b w.r.t. the last variable T, or -1 if not (i.e., f(0,...,0,T) is zero).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works for any monomial ordering. Example: returns 2 for given polynomial. (From weierstr.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: rootsmr.lib overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview: rootsmr.lib contains routines for counting the number of real roots of multivariate polynomial systems using two methods: deterministic computation via signature of a bilinear form (nrRootsDeterm) and a rational univariate projection with a pseudorandom polynomial (nrRootsProbab).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes commands to verify correctness of probabilistic answers and references. (From rootsmr.lib introduction.)
